requirements.title: Unhandled end-of-record initiates error termination
requirements.definition: An EOR condition in an I/O statement containing neither EOR= nor IOSTAT= initiates error termination.

pending.eor-without-eor-or-iostat-terminates: In a subprocess fixture, first create a short external formatted record, then perform nonadvancing input past it without EOR= or IOSTAT=; assert abnormal termination without comparing diagnostic text.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. requirements.title: Handled end-of-record applies pad-mode effects
requirements.definition: When EOR occurs with EOR= or IOSTAT= present and no error occurs, PAD=YES pads the record with blanks to satisfy the effective item and data edit descriptors that require more characters, while PAD=NO makes the effective item undefined.

pending.handled-eor-pad-yes-blanks: Create a short external formatted record, prefill the target with nonblank sentinels, use nonadvancing input with PAD="YES" and an edit descriptor requiring more characters, and assert only the blank-padded characters and IOSTAT_EOR.
pending.handled-eor-pad-no-effective-item-undefi: No portable oracle may inspect an effective item that PAD="NO" makes undefined; future tests assert IOSTAT_EOR and avoid using the item afterward.

requirements.title: Handled end-of-record terminates input processing and positions after the current record
requirements.definition: Handled EOR terminates input-list processing, positions the input file after the current record, and defines IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, and SIZE= specifiers that appear as specified by their owning rules.

pending.handled-eor-input-processing-terminates: Use nonadvancing input on a short first record before a known second record, assert IOSTAT_EOR, and avoid relying on later input-list items that are not completed.
pending.handled-eor-position-after-current-recor: After provoking EOR on the first of two known records, perform the next advancing READ and assert it returns the second record, proving positioning after the current record.
pending.handled-eor-iostat-defined: Initialize IOSTAT to zero, provoke nonadvancing EOR, and assert the named constant IOSTAT_EOR rather than its numeric value.
pending.handled-eor-iomsg-defined: No portable oracle compares IOMSG text or proves an assigned message differs from a sentinel; future EOR tests use IOSTAT_EOR/EOR= for portable observation.
pending.handled-eor-size-defined: Initialize SIZE to a negative sentinel, provoke nonadvancing EOR after transferring known characters, and assert the value specified by 12.6.2.16 for that transfer.

requirements.title: Handled end-of-record makes transfer do-variables undefined
requirements.definition: For a data transfer statement or wait-operation EOR, do-variables in the initiating statement become undefined.

pending.handled-eor-do-variables-undefined: No portable oracle may inspect a do-variable that the source makes undefined; future EOR tests do not use it after the condition.

requirements.title: EOR= branches on handled end-of-record
requirements.definition: If an EOR= specifier appears for handled EOR, execution branches to the statement with the specified label.

pending.handled-eor-eor-branch: Initialize a marker to a nonmatching sentinel, provoke nonadvancing EOR with EOR= and IOSTAT=, set the marker only at the EOR target, and assert the marker and IOSTAT_EOR.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.10.3-12.12: IOLENGTH, error, end-of-record and end-of-file conditions, IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, and restrictions on I/O statements (batch166). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer, accepted with no findings. IOLENGTH's exact count is latitude but its direct-access RECL= suitability is planned; END=/EOR= conditions, IOSTAT_END and IOSTAT_EOR distinctness, zero on success and positive errors are planned portably; IOMSG unchanged on success is planned with a sentinel while condition-message text is never compared. Source accounting only.
